story: Born in a prison in Mathura and carried across the Yamuna to Gokul, Krishna grew up as a cowherd who stole butter, played the flute, and lifted Govardhan hill to shelter his village from Indra's storm. Later he killed his tyrant uncle Kamsa, ruled Dwarka, and drove Arjuna's chariot at Kurukshetra, where he taught him the Bhagavad Gita.
belief: Krishna is worshipped as the eighth avatar of Vishnu, and many Vaishnavas see him as the supreme god himself. His central teaching in the Gita is to do your duty without clinging to its results.
turns: In the war he bent the rules again and again: the half-lie that brought down Drona, the moment chosen to kill Karna, and the signal for Bhima to strike Duryodhana below the waist. Gandhari cursed him for not stopping the war, and his own Yadava clan later destroyed itself.
facts: Janmashtami celebrates his birth at midnight.
The Bhagavad Gita has 700 verses in 18 chapters.
ISKCON, the Hare Krishna movement, has carried his worship around the world.
